summary: Georg Buddruss was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Paul Thieme at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1950–1954) and later at the University of Tübingen (~1954–1956). From 1963 to 1995, he served as professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.

Georg Bühler worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen (1855–1858), studying under Benfey, Sauppe, Curtius, and Ewald. He held posts at Elphinstone College and Mumbai (~1863–1880) and the University of Vienna (from 1880).
Georg Christoph Lichtenberg worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1763 to 1769 and held an academic post there from circa 1769 until 1799.

Linguist Georg Curtius studied at Bonn under Lassen, Schlegel, and Ritschl, and in Berlin under Bopp. He held posts at Berlin (1845–1849), Charles University (1849–1854), Kiel University (1854–1862), and Leipzig University (1862–1885).
Georg Forster was an Indologist who studied at Saint Peter's School. He held posts at Vilnius University from 1784 to 1787 and at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from circa 1788 to 1792.

Georg Friedrich Grotefend was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied at the Lessing-Gymnasium and at the University of Göttingen circa 1795–1797.

Georg Huth worked in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Leipzig University from circa 1885 to 1889 and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1891 to 1906.

Linguist and historian Georg Kaibel held posts at the University of Rostock (~1879–1882), University of Breslau (~1882–1883), University of Greifswald (~1883–1886), and University of Göttingen (~1897–1901).

Linguist Georg Ludolf Dissen studied at the University of Göttingen (~1803–1807). He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1811–1813) and the University of Göttingen (~1813–1837).

Georg Martin Dursch was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1818–1823) and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy at the University of Paris (~1826–1828), becoming professor at Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen in 1829.

Georg Morgenstierne was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sten Konow, Heinrich Lüders, and Wilhelm Schulze, completing a Promotion in Berlin. He was a professor at the University of Gothenburg (1930) and the University of Oslo (1937–1962).
Georg Simmel was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1876 to 1881. He later held an academic post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1885 to 1914.

Georg Wilhelm Freytag was a linguist who studied at Göttingen (~1807–1811) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (~1815–1819). He served as a repetent at Göttingen (1811–1813) and as professor of oriental languages at Bonn (1819–1861).

Philosopher Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel studied at Tübingen, the Tübinger Stift, and Jena under Schelling. He held academic posts at Jena (~1801–1807), Heidelberg (~1816–1818), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1818–1831).

Georg von Simson worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Mainz (~1953–1957) and Göttingen (~1957–1974). He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1968–1977) and as professor at the University of Oslo (1977–2003).

Georg von der Gabelentz worked in Sinology and linguistics, studying at Jena, Leipzig, and TU Dresden. He served as professor of East Asian languages at Leipzig (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1889), joining the Prussian Academy of Sciences in 1889.

George A. Kennedy was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1937) under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke, and later held a post at Yale University from circa 1935 to 1960.

George A. Keyworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., Ronald Egan, Shuizhao Wang, and William F. Powell. He held posts at Colorado (2001) and Saskatchewan (attested 2019).

George Abraham Grierson worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1868–1871), served in the Indian Civil Service (~1871–1898), was Superintendent of the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and governed SOAS (1917–1925).

Indologist George Baumann earned his PhD at Heidelberg University (~1968–1973) and studied at Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen (~1973–1975). From 1976 to 2001, he was affiliated with the University of Tübingen and served at Tübingen University Library.
